preamble: The spelling of several well-known (but undefined) entries is incorrect, which may not be to your taste!

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's article page and its grid picture, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Launch battery-powered vehicle

definitions.meaning: to launch a company or a boat is to set it going on the market or the water
the electric milk cart that delivered milk to British doorsteps

explanation.definitionFit: To float a company launches it on the stock market; a milk float is an electric delivery van in Britain.

clue.text: Around old vehicle stick first of labels

indicators.note: the stick goes round the outside of the other two pieces, its first letter before them

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
a coach is a bus-like road vehicle

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word labels is used

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a label on an old vehicle, the first job of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like a verb (glue on a label); it is a walking stick. The entry misspells the French fashion designer's first name as the hot drink, as the preamble warns.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble leaves the famous person undefined: the entry is a fashion designer's name misspelt with a hot chocolate drink.

clue.text: I love going through rubbish in port

indicators.note: the I-plus-rubbish group sits inside the name of the port, after its first letter

parts.note: Poole is a harbour town on the Dorset coast of southern England

indicators.note: the zero for love passes into the middle of the rubbish word

parts.note: tat is cheap, shoddy goods
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to rummaging through the rubbish in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'port' as wine or a harbour in general; it is the Dorset town. The entry turns an Irish actor's first name into a flatbread, as the preamble warns.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble leaves the famous person undefined: the entry is a Lawrence of Arabia actor's name with a flatbread for his first name.

clue.text: See 3
1930s' King of Hollywood introduces himself as Asian flower

indicators.note: the ape introducing himself says the word for himself before his name

parts.note: a speaker referring to himself says me
King Kong, the giant ape of the 1933 Hollywood film

explanation.surface: Clark Gable, the 1930s King of Hollywood, introduces himself as a flower from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King of Hollywood' wants to be Clark Gable; it is King Kong, half the name. A 'flower' in crosswords is a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is a crossword name for a river, and this one runs through south-east Asia from Tibet to Vietnam.

clue.text: Holy chamber where racists contrived the ultimate in blasphemy

indicators.note: the letters of racists are contrived, worked into a new arrangement
only the final letter of blasphemy is used

explanation.surface: Bigots blaspheme in a church's sacred room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' turns RACISTS into SACRIST, and 'the ultimate in' blasphemy adds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy is the room in a church where sacred vessels and vestments are kept, a holy chamber.

clue.text: Relatives on the toilet to investigate

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: loo is British slang for the toilet
kin are one's relatives
taken as written

explanation.surface: Family members sitting on the lavatory are being looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'to' of the last two words belongs to the wordplay, leaving 'investigate' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into a matter is an idiom for examining or investigating it.

clue.text: Fervent devotion lessened, keeping elderly woman in women's quarters

indicators.note: the shortened devotion word holds the old woman inside it
the word for fervent devotion is reduced by losing its final letter

parts.note: zeal is fervent enthusiasm or devotion
nan is a grandmother, an elderly woman

explanation.surface: A grandmother lives in the women's part of a house where religious fervour has cooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lessened' cuts ZEAL to ZEA, which by 'keeping' holds NAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In India and Iran a zenana is the part of a house kept for the women of the household.

clue.text: See 24 across
Being extravagantly macabre, suffered from mild dose of wind?

parts.note: got as in got the flu, suffered from an illness
hic is the sound of a hiccup, a small bout of wind

explanation.surface: A gloomy, horror-loving person had a touch of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' wants to be weather; it is the digestive kind, a hiccup.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic fiction and style dwell on the gloomy, grotesque and extravagantly horrific.

clue.text: A noisy abbreviated function — it's the fruit!

indicators.note: the noisy word is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: vocal means loud and outspoken
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A loud, short party is held for the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbreviated' trims VOCAL to VOCA; 'function' is a party, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped fruit from the tropics has green flesh and one large stone.

clue.text: Done or undone, container ultimately awaiting delivery

indicators.note: the letters of done or are undone and put back in another arrangement
only the last letter of container is used

explanation.surface: A delivery waits as to whether the container job is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' turns DONEOR into ONORDE, and 'ultimately' adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that have been ordered but not yet delivered are said to be on order, an idiom of retail.

clue.text: Moronic soap, I gather

indicators.note: something moronic is muddled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that a soap opera is idiotic, so they hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moronic' rearranges SOAPIGATHER. The entry is the Greek mathematician spelt with a pie in it, as the preamble warns.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble leaves the famous person undefined: the entry is the Greek geometer of triangle fame, misspelt to include a baked dish.

clue.text: Don't open box — aim for a hole, perhaps?

indicators.note: the box word is not opened, losing its first letter

parts.note: to spar is to box with an opponent

explanation.surface: A warning not to open a box, with golf in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container; it is the verb, to spar. 'Don't open' removes its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers aim to complete each hole in a set number of strokes, the standard score for that hole.

clue.text: Old queen not entirely happy about gold given to Scotsman

indicators.note: the shortened happy word goes round the gold-and-Scotsman pair
the word for happy loses its last letter

parts.note: glad means happy
or is gold in heraldry
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A former queen is less than pleased when gold is handed to a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry gold is 'or', a crossword staple; the happy word loses only its last letter before wrapping the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloriana was the poetic name for Queen Elizabeth I of England, a former queen.

clue.text: Element of predator and prey?

parts.note: a wolf is a hunting predator
a ram, a male sheep, is the sort of animal a wolf preys on

explanation.surface: A question about a natural element linking hunter and hunted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' looks like a part of the food chain; it is a chemical element, another name for tungsten.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is an older name for tungsten, the chemical element with symbol W.

clue.text: Here a parliamentary official's behind court process, finally plugging deficiency

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: the final letter fills a gap inside the deficiency word

parts.note: lack is a deficiency or shortage

indicators.note: only the last letter of process is used

explanation.surface: Behind the court proceedings, a parliamentary officer plugs a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal; it means woo. 'finally' gives S, which 'plugging' sets inside LACK after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Woolsack is the wool-stuffed seat in the House of Lords on which the Lord Speaker sits.

clue.text: Psycho murderer, in the morning, getting up

indicators.note: in a down answer, getting up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer
am stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A psychopathic killer rises early.
explanation.walkthrough: CAIN plus AM, all read upwards because of 'getting up', makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A psycho is a madman or homicidal lunatic, the same as a raving madman.

clue.text: Protection with egg on one's face, might you say?

indicators.note: signals that the words are said aloud to sound like another

parts.note: custardy jokingly means covered in custard, an egg-based sauce, as after a custard pie in the face

explanation.surface: A quip about protective care for someone left embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on one's face' is an idiom for embarrassment, but here it is literal custard, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in custody is being kept in protective care or guardianship.

clue.text: Knowledgeable? Not very very, for example

indicators.note: two Vs, each the abbreviation for very, are removed

parts.note: savvy means shrewd and knowledgeable

explanation.surface: Someone is barely clued up, to take an instance.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the standard abbreviation for very, so 'very very' names two Vs to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as in 'take, say, the Romans', it introduces an instance, just like for example.

clue.text: Fine bloody mess with finery

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
raw meat is bloody and uncooked

indicators.note: the letters of finery are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A gory mess is fine, alongside the glad rags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' scrambles FINERY into INFREY. The entry swaps the talk-show host's first name for a vegetable, as the preamble warns.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble leaves the famous person undefined: the entry is the US talk-show host's name with a pod vegetable for her first name.

clue.text: See 25 across
War commander marched primarily into capital, that of Latvia?

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the capital city's name

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

indicators.note: only the first letter of marched is used

parts.note: the capital letter, or initial, of Latvia is L

explanation.surface: A general marched first into the capital of Latvia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that of Latvia' reuses the sense of capital as a capital letter: the initial of Latvia.
explanation.definitionFit: Erwin Rommel was the German field marshal of the Second World War known as the Desert Fox.

clue.text: Reddish-yellow, sunny extremes?

definitions.meaning: the colour of sand, light brownish-yellow, as of hair
read as the two outer letters of the word sunny joined by the conjunction for plus

explanation.surface: The colour of a sunny day at its outer edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading spells out the outer letters of 'sunny' with the word for plus between them; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy hair is a light reddish-yellow, the colour of sand.

clue.text: Toy with a desert basin

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

explanation.surface: Messing about in a dry lake bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A playa is a flat, dry lake bed in a desert, which floods only after rare rain.

clue.text: A cultural festival within reach, snored uncontrollably

indicators.note: the A and festival word sit inside the reach word before its final two letters

parts.note: span is the reach or extent of something
a mela is a South Asian fair or cultural festival

indicators.note: the letters of snored are jumbled without control

explanation.surface: At an arts festival nearby, someone snored uncontrollably.
explanation.walkthrough: A mela is a South Asian festival, common at British Asian community events. The actress's first name is spelt with tinned meat, as the preamble warns.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble leaves the famous person undefined: the entry is the Baywatch actress's name misspelt with a tinned pork product.

clue.text: Underground worker keeps circulating awhile in church

indicators.note: the underground worker holds the rest inside him, after his first two letters

parts.note: a miner works underground

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the letters of awhile circulate into a new order

explanation.surface: A miner keeps walking round for a while in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests the London Tube; it is a mine. The film director's surname is spelt as a frankfurter sausage, as the preamble warns.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble leaves the famous person undefined: the entry is the Death Wish director's name misspelt with a frankfurter sausage.

clue.text: Swimmer with a tail, barred?

parts.note: a cod is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A fish with a tail that is barred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' looks like stripes on the tail; it means set in musical bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a musical work, a tail end written in bars.

clue.text: See 2 down
Page one added another story in the end

indicators.note: another version of the letters, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I

indicators.note: only the final letter of story is used

explanation.surface: A page is added to a tale, with another twist in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges I plus ADDED into EADIDD, and 'in the end' gives Y. The rapper's initial is spelt as a vegetable, as the preamble warns.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble leaves the famous person undefined: the entry is the US rapper and producer's name with a green vegetable for his initial.
